Chassis perimeter.rationale: The bumper ring and the perimeter rules bound the robot; strike loads must reach the module stations. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Bumper ring.purpose: Protects the frame perimeter in contact with field elements and robots.
Bumper ring.rationale: Required bumpers; the ring follows the actual frame plan hull. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Power distribution hub.purpose: Distributes battery power to the controllers and the control system.
Power distribution hub.rationale: Every load in the voltage budget draws through it. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

roboRIO 2.purpose: Runs the robot program, the eject interlock and the drive control.
roboRIO 2.rationale: A control computer is required. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

VH-109 radio.purpose: Links the robot to the driver station and field.
VH-109 radio.rationale: Required communications. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Main 120 A breaker.purpose: Disconnects and protects the main battery circuit.
Main 120 A breaker.rationale: Required main disconnect; reset path checked in service-breaker-reset. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Nip controller (SPARK MAX).rationale: Uses the pan controller's placement on the equipment sheet. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Chassis battery plug and bracket.purpose: Mates the battery SB50 to the robot-side main leads.
Chassis battery plug and bracket.rationale: The battery disconnects at a plug the plug-grip hand can reach. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Main power loom.purpose: Reserves the main lead route from the SB50 to the breaker and PDH.
Main power loom.rationale: The main leads must avoid the battery lift and the plug grip. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Branch and CAN trunk.purpose: Reserves the branch power and CAN route to the controllers.
Branch and CAN trunk.rationale: Branch and CAN wiring cross the centre gap above the crossmembers. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Module 1 lead reserve.purpose: Reserves the module 1 motor and CANcoder leads under the equipment sheet.
Module 1 lead reserve.rationale: Module leads must leave the housing clear of the steer sweep. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Module 2 lead reserve.purpose: Reserves the module 2 motor and CANcoder leads under the equipment sheet.
Module 2 lead reserve.rationale: Module leads must leave the housing clear of the steer sweep. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Module 4 lead reserve.rationale: Module leads must leave the housing clear of the steer sweep. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Battery tray and retention.purpose: Supports and retains the battery case below the sills.
Battery tray and retention.rationale: The battery sits low and central and lifts out through the centre gap. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Dressed battery.material: Sealed lead-acid FRC battery with leads (excluded by R103)
Dressed battery.purpose: Supplies the robot; its case, leads and battery-side SB50 move together in service.
Dressed battery.rationale: The pack is the voltage source of the budget. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Breaker reset hand.purpose: Clearance gauge for a hand reaching the main breaker reset from above.
Breaker reset hand.rationale: Resetting the breaker must not need the pocket removed. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Plug grip hand.purpose: Clearance gauge for a hand gripping the SB50 pair.
Plug grip hand.rationale: The battery swap starts with this disconnect. Carried forward from the iteration 002 baseline as a revisable premise.

Pocket tray.material: 1/8 in polycarbonate with a UHMW contact face (proposal)
Pocket tray.purpose: Receives the station pipe on a 52.3 deg chute, rolls it down the 15.74 deg floor and holds it between two walls 10 mm clear of its ends.
Pocket tray.rationale: A fixed path replaces the pan's moving receiver; the 15.74 deg floor keeps the seated pipe pressed toward the nip at 0.27 g and the walls square its 301.6 mm length.

Hood (removable).purpose: Caps the pocket 10 mm above the pipe so a rebound cannot lift it, and carries the check-flap pin.
Hood (removable).rationale: Isolation: without it 4/4 adverse receives still seat (peak rise with it 0.74 mm), so the trials do not show it earning its place; it is kept as the flap carrier and a bound on an unmodelled pipe-end or yawed bounce, and lifts off for the pit unload path.

Check flap.material: 1/16 in polycarbonate, steel pin and torsion spring (proposal)
Check flap.purpose: Lets the arriving pipe in and stops it rolling back up the floor when the chassis accelerates toward the reef.
Check flap.rationale: Isolation: without it a gently settled pipe is lost rearward at 8 g (1/2 retained; 3 g 2/2); with it every worm-locked sled case is retained.

Port nip side plate.purpose: Carries the port bearings of both rollers, the worm drive and the lip hinge, and lands the cassette on the port stringer.
Port nip side plate.rationale: The nip is the pocket's front stop and must hold its 12 mm squeeze and the 0.4-0.5 kN receive bite load.

Starboard nip side plate.purpose: Carries the starboard bearings, the coupling belt and idler, the latch servo and the lip hinge.
Starboard nip side plate.rationale: Paired with the port plate it makes the nip a removable cassette.

Lower nip roller.material: 2 in 35A compliant wheels on 1/2 in hollow hex (COTS)
Lower nip roller.purpose: Lower half of the nip: front stop on receive, driven eject roller, and the roller the pipe rolls over onto the lip.
Lower nip roller.rationale: With the upper roller it replaces the evaluation's fence, which no nip could lift the pipe over (finding PD1).

Upper nip roller.material: 2 in 35A compliant wheels on 1/2 in hollow hex (COTS)
Upper nip roller.purpose: Upper half of the nip: clamps the pipe in the bite and drives it through the throat.
Upper nip roller.rationale: A two-sided squeeze moves the pipe without spin and holds it in the bite when the worm locks.

Nip worm reducer and NEO 550.material: NEO 550 and a self-locking worm reducer (article not selected)
Nip worm reducer and NEO 550.purpose: Drives the lower roller through a self-locking worm, so the unpowered nip cannot be back-driven.
Nip worm reducer and NEO 550.rationale: Isolation: with free-turning rollers 3/4 adverse receives seat (the rest pass through the nip); locked, 16/16 seat. At 9 V it still drives the pipe through the squeeze (slowest 0.44 m/s in the nip).

Nip coupling belt.material: Timing belt, pulleys and idler (article not selected)
Nip coupling belt.purpose: Counter-rotates the upper roller from the lower shaft.
Nip coupling belt.rationale: Both rollers must turn so the pipe leaves the throat without spin and the worm locks both.

Seated-pipe sensor.purpose: Reports a seated, displaced or missing pipe from the hood top.
Seated-pipe sensor.rationale: The narrative requires detecting displacement or loss, and the eject interlock needs pipe presence (gate G5).

Lip-deployed switch.purpose: Reports that the lip reached its deployed stop.
Lip-deployed switch.rationale: The eject interlock must not run the nip into a stowed lip (latch-failed control).

Lip latch servo.material: Hobby-class servo and steel pin (article not selected)
Lip latch servo.purpose: Holds the upright stowed lip for the starting configuration and releases it once at match start.
Lip latch servo.rationale: R102 needs the lip inside the perimeter at the start; the deploy happens on the field.

Deployable exit lip.material: 1/8 in polycarbonate, hinge pin and torsion spring (proposal)
Deployable exit lip.purpose: Rolls the ejected pipe off a tip 100 mm beyond the frame line at 0.55 m so it drops into the trough.
Deployable exit lip.rationale: Isolation: with the lip removed the 12 V eject is captured at 0 and 50 mm stand-off and lost at 75 and 100 mm; deployed, 80/80 G2 ejects over 0-100 mm are captured and supported after withdrawal. A latch failure (lip still up) blocks the exit.

Rear inlet upright port.purpose: Carries the inlet walls at the station face from the rear perimeter.
Rear inlet upright port.rationale: The 0.8 m inlet lip is far above any chassis member.

Floor post port.purpose: Supports the pocket floor from the port upper stringer.
Floor post port.rationale: The floor spans 650 mm between the inlet and the nip and needs a mid support.

Rear inlet upright starboard.purpose: Carries the inlet walls at the station face from the rear perimeter.

Floor post starboard.purpose: Supports the pocket floor from the starboard upper stringer.

CORAL pipe.purpose: The finite game piece followed from the station chute through receive, carry, eject, the lip and the trough.
CORAL pipe.rationale: The role scores two station pipes in the L1 trough; every clearance and trial uses its actual diameter and length.

L1 trough sector A (field).material: Reef L1 trough section (field element, not robot)
L1 trough sector A (field).purpose: Field fixture: the red L1 trough section the pipe must land in and stay supported in.
L1 trough sector A (field).rationale: The delivery interaction is checked against the registered trough section at the shown 50 mm dock.

provisional.seated-pipe sensor: Not placed: needed by the eject interlock (RR3)
provisional.lip-deployed sensor: Not placed: needed by the eject interlock (RR3)

narrativeReview.read: Read end to end on 2026-11-22: LEAVE, two TELEOP station-to-L1 cycles in sectors A and B, custody, trough release and support, park, the endgame choice and the empty-start fallback. commissioning.md restates the two-pipe objective.

objectives.objective: AUTO: leave the starting line with the whole occupied robot (3 points)
objectives.basis: A field-route objective for the empty robot; this package reserves the stowed starting configuration (886.7 mm tall, lip inside the perimeter) and deploys the lip at match start (lip-deploy) but places no starting-line fixture.

objectives.objective: TELEOP: take one station-issued CORAL from the red station
objectives.basis: Cases receive-chute to flap-close; receive trials (field-trials.json, G1 model); premises station-receive-face, station-arrival-speed and receive-seat-time.

objectives.objective: Carry it to the red reef while crossing peer routes
objectives.basis: Case loaded-carry; sled trials 1-8 g both directions; weak-pack voltage premise. A peer contact on the forward lip is not loaded (PD7).

objectives.objective: Sustain a deliverable load: keep custody when accelerating, braking or contacted, and detect displacement or loss
objectives.basis: Case loaded-carry and the sled trials (every worm-locked case retained); the seated-pipe sensor and lip-deployed switch are placed reserves. Physical retention and detection are verification gates per docs/preliminary-design.md line 57 ('retention ... and physical performance require their own commissioned evidence'): G3 (60/60 retained, kill on any loss at <= 3 g) and G5 (every displaced or missing pipe flagged within 50 ms, no false loss); tread stiffness PD2 is measured first.

objectives.objective: Release into the intended L1 trough sector A, clear the wall and leave the pipe supported after withdrawal
objectives.basis: Cases eject-throat to trough-landing against the placed trough fixture; eject trials capture the pipe and assess support 2 s after a 120 mm withdrawal at every 0-100 mm stand-off; field-interaction.html plays them with the latch-failed control.

objectives.objective: Return for a second station CORAL and score it in sector B with the first pipe as an obstacle
objectives.basis: The cycle resets (empty pocket, lip stays deployed) and the same eject cases apply at sector B; evidence/sector-b-check.json places the first pipe at its sector-A rest pose (471 mm across) and measures the robot and the second pipe's release path against it. The cycle rehearsal credits a second L1 delivery at every rehearsed receive time. The sector divider panel is not modelled.

objectives.objective: PARK: reserve the south lane, stow, reach the zone and stop
objectives.basis: Case withdraw-park; the lip stays deployed (it has no in-match stow), which the park envelope and R105 premise both include.

objectives.objective: Endgame alternatives: shallow or deep CAGE

objectives.basis: The same robot with no pipe aboard; lip-deploy and withdraw-park need no pipe.

objectives.objective: Partner and station dependence: Red 1 station change and station depletion
objectives.basis: An alliance-chain comparison owned by conceptual design; it changes no package volume.
